newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong business, labour back rights curbs laws.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong business, labour back rights curbs laws.

text.p: Hong Kong government officials, businessmen and union leaders on Friday proposed scrapping a set of labour rights laws recently suspended by the territory's China-appointed legislature.

The government-appointed Labour Advisory Board, which advises the authorities on labour issues, recommended scrapping two laws, one on collective bargaining and the other banning discrimination against union members by employers.
However, another law on the use of trade union funds would be amended after the board, which groups business, unions and government, reached a decision, a government statement said.
Last month, the Beijing-backed Provisional Legislature endorsed government bills freezing the three laws until October on grounds that they may hurt Hong Kong's competitiveness.
The move sparked an outcry from pro-democracy trade unions in Hong Kong and labour groups world-wide, which bombarded the territory's leader Tung Chee-hwa with letters of protest.
The development was the latest in a series of moves to cut back democracy and civil liberties in the territory of 6.4 million people that Britain handed back to China on July 1.
